case.title: Disputed delivery of order ORD-1042
case.question: The customer says order ORD-1042 never arrived, but carrier tracking says it was delivered. What happened to the parcel?

hypotheses.statement: The carrier delivered the parcel to the customer's address; any loss happened after delivery.
The carrier delivered the parcel to the wrong address.
The parcel never left the warehouse.

configuration.speck: Evidence Desk as built: one Speck case carried across the stages on a temporary Speck database (the case on the page is not touched). Each stage's new records are assessed and Speck's beliefs revised; a record replaced by a later one stops counting and the beliefs that rested on it are rebuilt.
configuration.stateless: The evaluation's stateless model baseline: at each stage, one call to the same Nemotron endpoint with the question, the explanations and every visible record (its text, its facts, and "replaces …" where the source says so). It keeps nothing between stages.
configuration.labels: No pre-registered labels: this case is not an evaluation case.

speck.headline: The carrier delivered the parcel to the customer's address; any loss happened after delivery.
reasons: Speck holds H-DELIVERED as supported at 0.788, at or above its supported threshold of 0.6.

support.rationale: Order placed and shipped to the customer's address.
Parcel scanned onto carrier manifest MAN-5521.
Carrier API confirms delivery at 14:02 AEDT on 13 Oct.
Customer reports non-receipt despite delivery claim.

explanation.text: The parcel was delivered to the customer's address on 13 Oct 2026 at 14:02 AEDT by driver D-219, as confirmed by the carrier tracking API (EV-CAR-003). The order was placed and shipped on 10 Oct 2026, and the parcel was scanned onto carrier manifest MAN-5521 (EV-OMS-001, EV-WMS-002). The customer support inbox (EV-SUP-004) indicates the customer did not receive it despite the delivery claim. No evidence supports misdelivery or non-shipment, so the parcel was delivered but may have been lost after delivery.

stateless.rationale: The carrier tracking API confirms delivery at 14:02 AEDT on 13 Oct, and the warehouse system shows the parcel was scanned onto the carrier manifest. The customer's non-receipt is likely due to post-delivery loss.

notes: Both approaches saw the same records at every stage, the same question and explanations, and the same assessor configuration.

Speck counts a conclusion only when it holds it as supported; a leading or pointed-to explanation is tentative. The stateless baseline has no such threshold beyond answering "unresolved" (model) or a tie or non-positive score (rules).

Differences come from Speck's explicit evidence and revision state and its conclusion policy (thresholds, decisive refutation, supersession), not from persistence alone: the evaluation's speck-fresh system, which rebuilds from scratch each time, reaches the same conclusions as speck-desk.

Live: model judgments vary between runs. This is one sample, not a rate. Speck calls the model per evidence chunk plus once for its explanation; the baseline calls it once per stage, so call counts and latency are not like for like.

Speck caps model-judged evidence at reliability 0.4, so Speck's own confidence rarely reaches its 0.6 threshold live. Since Build 4 Evidence Desk can still conclude by corroboration (two or more source systems agree, nothing recorded against, every rival ruled out or unsupported); each such conclusion is marked, with Speck's own confidence beside it.
